content.title: About
content.content: Pudding is a smooth dessert made from milk, cream and thickeners, often flavored with varieties other than chocolate. The range includes vanilla, caramel, berry, coffee and coconut options. Pudding is served chilled, frequently topped with fruit, nuts or sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pudding has ancient roots: early recipes appear in Roman cuisine.
Unlike jelly, pudding thickens with starch, gelatin or egg yolk.
In Japan, “mochi‑puddings” incorporate glutinous rice flour for a chewy texture.
Vegan versions are made with plant milk and agar‑agar.
Pudding is often used as a base for cakes and dessert parfaits.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Depending on the flavor, pudding can contain B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible protein
items.content: Egg yolk or milk adds a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: Probiotic content
items.content: When yogurt or kefir is used, pudding can help maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low‑sugar options
items.content: Sugar can be replaced with stevia or erythritol, lowering the glycemic impact.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy should choose plant‑based versions.

items.title: High sugar content in traditional recipes
items.content: Excess sugar may contribute to weight gain and increase cavity risk.

items.title: Thickener additives
items.content: Some artificial thickeners can cause intolerance in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Pudding made with cream can be calorie‑rich; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pudding chilled in individual glasses or bowls, garnished with berries, fruit sauces, nuts, honey or sprinkles. It can be layered in cakes, used as a filling for pastries, or enjoyed as a light evening dessert.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared pudding in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized containers; thaw in the fridge before serving and gently stir if needed.
